parts.t: Bradner is a rural community in the northwest corner of Abbotsford, named after Thomas Bradner, who settled around 1895. Most of the land is farmed, and the Fraser River forms the northern edge of the area.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 12, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate since 2015. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Abbotsford and the Agricultural Land Commission.
This page is not legal, planning or financial advice. Whether you are buying or selling in Bradner, start by checking the zoning, the community plan and the schools that serve the address.

blocks.text: Planning and the ALR in Bradner

parts.t: Bradner is rural, so the City’s Official Community Plan (OCP) and the ALR rules apply property by property.

Where a well supplies the house, find out how much water it produces and how clean that water is, and request any earlier test results.
Find out how old the system is and when it was last serviced, and have it inspected.
Ask whether barns, shops, arenas and suites were built with permits.
Ask what claims or restrictions others may have over the property: covenants, rights of way, easements, and the access you rely on.
Building close to a stream is restricted, which can limit where a home can go. Any watercourse on or close to the property is something to raise with the City of Abbotsford.
